patterns: THE ONE REPEATING DEFECT — the list-wearing-a-sentence. An enumeration of three or four peer items is written as one sentence joined by semicolons, usually introduced by a colon and a counting phrase ('Two details worth knowing:', 'Two notes on the current toolchain:', 'When a store library earns its cost:', 'What a store library costs, stated plainly:', 'Practical Angular specifics:'). This single habit produces most of the over-limit sentences in both locales and every sentence above 40 words: q-9, q-22, q-33, q-45, q-48, q-50, q-57, q-71, q-91. It is not tier-bound — it appears in junior entries as often as advanced ones. The fix is mechanical and does not touch a single technical claim: the same items become a bullet list, which the bank already uses correctly in dozens of other answers ('Two properties matter:', 'Three practical points:', 'Key fields:'). Fixing this one pattern would take the English over-limit rate from 18.2% to roughly single digits.

SECOND PATTERN — the closing pitfall paragraph is where sentences go long. Every one of the 104 answers ends with a '**Common pitfall:** / **Частая ловушка:**' paragraph, and it is consistently the densest paragraph in the answer: the flags list 4 of the 4 longest paragraphs in each locale as pitfall paragraphs (q-5, q-6, q-10, q-16, q-17), and the longest sentences in q-58, q-76, q-102, q-66, q-99, q-40 are all inside one. The cause is that the paragraph does four jobs in a row with no break: name the mistake, explain the mechanism, describe the observable symptom, give the fix. Splitting it after the mechanism — or letting the symptom be its own sentence — would leave the content identical.

WHAT THIS BANK DOES RIGHT, and should feed the style guide. (1) Answer-first is near-perfect: the median answer lead is 12 words in Russian and 13.5 in English, and it states the mechanism in the first clause — '`track` сообщает Angular, как опознать элемент между рендерами', '`@if` встроен в синтаксис шаблона', 'A signal is a container for a value that knows who reads it'. Only 1 of 104 answers warms up instead of answering (q-17). (2) Structure is 100% uniform: every single answer has at least one code block (average 1.6, never zero) and every single answer ends with a concrete, named pitfall that describes the *symptom* as the reader would experience it ('баг выглядит как проблема кеширования', 'the symptom looks like a state bug and sends people debugging the wrong component') rather than just stating a rule. (3) The React bridge is explicit and repeated rather than assumed: roughly 20 answers name the React habit that misfires ('это привычка из useEffect', 'the way a React developer might pass a setter down'), which is precisely right for this audience. (4) Legacy is quarantined into 7 blockquotes ('> В легаси увидишь...') instead of being interleaved with current API, so a reader never has to disambiguate which version they are reading about. Density of 12.0 flags per 1k words is genuine, not an artefact.

RUSSIAN IS THE STRONGER LOCALE and is close to a model for the site. Register is uniform «ты» across all 104 answers and all four difficulty tiers (no «вы»/«ты» drift of the kind found in nextjs). Zero «осуществляется», zero «данный», zero «в случае если»; only 5 uses of «является», all idiomatic ('шаблон не является JavaScript'). Terminology is confidently domesticated rather than calqued — «инпут», «аутпут», «бочка» for barrel file, «вью пачкается», «схлопывает» for coalesce, «дёргается» for jank — which reads as written-in-Russian, not translated.
notes: NO DIFFICULTY SEAM. Unlike typescript and nextjs, quality here is a smooth gradient, not a cliff. RU over-limit rate by tier: 3% / 4% / 8% / 5%; EN: 12% / 18% / 21% / 27% — a mild slope with no discontinuity at the junior/middle vs senior/advanced boundary. Every structural feature is uniform across all four tiers: 100% of answers have a code block (junior 24/24 through advanced 22/22), 100% have a Common pitfall paragraph, 0% use markdown headings anywhere (a consistent choice, not a senior-tier regression), and the RU «ты» register never shifts. Answer length grows sensibly with difficulty (171 to 233 words RU) rather than exploding. Secondary gaps: only 2 ASCII diagrams (q-57, q-63) and 1 table (q-27) across 104 answers, so 18 flagged theory walls — notably q-38, q-51, q-57, q-61, q-67, q-69 — have no visual anchor even where one would obviously help (interceptor chain order, injector resolution order, @defer trigger table). Rubric D would move from 4 to 5 with three or four more diagrams in the existing q-57 style. The single measurable locale asymmetry is sentence length, and it is caused almost entirely by the list-wearing-a-sentence pattern rather than by English vocabulary, which stays at B1-B2 apart from a handful of figurative phrases ('monkey-patched', 'blunt instrument', 'earns its cost', 'where it bites').
